A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Activated LoRA work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original aLoRA experiments on uncertainty quantification, answerability, query rewriting, and jailbreak detection, including numerical comparisons with LoRA.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds original vLLM timing measurements and supervised finetuning comparisons across seven tasks and four base models.

M1.justification: The token-selective low-rank architecture remains equivalent, but the reported activation boundary changes from the invocation sequence's start in v1 Section 3.1 to one token after its start in v3 Appendix A. v3 also discusses extending the same masking to MLP blocks beyond v1's stated Q/K/V-only implementation restriction, without reporting MLP experiments.

E1.justification: v3 adds seven SFT tasks covering Bengali hate-speech classification, WIQA effects, two MMLU subjects, SocialIQA and SuperGLUE question generation, and Hindi sentence perturbation. These substantially broaden languages and task requirements beyond v1's intrinsics, even where underlying datasets previously appeared as uncertainty-calibration sources. The original intrinsic evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Standard LoRA remains the evaluated comparison method for the retained intrinsics and the added SFT and timing experiments. Additional base models are experimental configurations; newly cited serving systems and external baselines do not become additional evaluated comparator methods.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a vLLM timing protocol across seven models, varying prompt length and one versus five evaluators, with fixed 256-token base answers, 16-token evaluations, and LoRA/aLoRA ranks of 8/32. Its new SFT protocol uses four epochs, validation-selected rank/learning-rate grids, and test accuracy with LLM judging for freeform outputs. Retained answerability and rewrite settings are preserved in Appendix G.

E4.justification: Figure 3 adds systematic latency-sensitivity analysis across prompt lengths, model sizes, and evaluator counts, distinguishing adapter-only from end-to-end costs. Appendix E also reports little timing change when adapter ranks are matched. v1 offered cache and capacity illustrations without measured scaling analysis; its existing standalone/non-standalone rewrite analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds an aggregate two-sided t-test for SFT accuracy differences, reporting p=0.8 at a 0.05 threshold, and specifies three consecutive batches per timing condition. Neither version provides systematic seed-based variability or confidence intervals. The 1,120 SFT training runs describe hyperparameter configurations, not repeated-seed replication.

E6.justification: v3 adds timing results reporting evaluator speedups up to 35 times and cross-model SFT results with a reported mean difference of 0.6 percentage points favoring LoRA. Retained uncertainty, answerability, and query-rewrite scores match v1. For jailbreak detection, LoRA accuracy changes from 0.944 to 0.943 and FPR from 0.009 to 0.011; its TPR and all aLoRA scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2 and Appendix C introduce propositions and proofs establishing pre-activation KV/internal-state equivalence for causal transformers and deriving computation and additional-memory costs, including multiple-adapter scaling. v1 contains the masked-update equation and informal cache-reuse reasoning but no corresponding formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of reusable base-model caches, modular intrinsics, and competitive LoRA accuracy remain. v3 presents working vLLM integration as a completed contribution, whereas v1's conclusion lists it as future work. Its introduction also explicitly extends the demonstrated accuracy claim to general SFT benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies v1's universal higher-rank observation to 'sometimes' and removes the figure-caption assurance that increasing rank eliminates any accuracy losses. It adds explanations of reverse input-cache reuse and workload-dependent end-to-end savings, discusses small-dataset/search variability, and explicitly identifies RL training and model-driven invocation as untested.

D1.justification: Appendices E–H add dataset/model identifiers, splits, hyperparameters, H100 hardware, vLLM batching instructions, and previously unstated jailbreak details, including 40,000 training samples and 5,000 Adam steps. Conversely, v3 replaces direct code links with a supplementary-code statement and removes v1's proprietary query-rewrite-data disclosure and hallucination-training recipe. Actual supplementary-code availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around scalable LoRA serving, long-context applications, agents, and general SFT benchmarks, adding discussion and citations such as S-LoRA, Compress Then Serve, vLLM, and SnapKV. v1's explicit sister-companion framing around Danilevsky et al. becomes a broader architecture narrative, with that work serving as the source of released intrinsic comparators and datasets.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the introduction and KV-cache background, incorporates v1's separate intrinsics/late-prompting section into the introduction, and reorganizes method and training exposition. It condenses intrinsic-specific subsections while moving invocation, capacity, usage, and experimental details into appendices. This substantially restructures retained material as well as accommodating new content.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the prompting and cache-flow diagrams and adds timing plots and an SFT results display. It merges v1 Tables 1–2 into Figure 6 and Tables 3–8 into Figure 7, relocates architecture/capacity illustrations to appendix Figures 9–10, and introduces tables surrounded by text. These are extensive display changes despite largely unchanged intrinsic scores.

improvement.justification: v1 asserts substantial inference savings without timing measurements; v3 directly tests this central claim on vLLM across seven models and workload sizes, backed by explicit cache-equivalence and cost proofs. Broader SFT comparisons also test generality beyond Granite intrinsics. These resolve an important validation gap. Small SFT test sets, incomplete uncertainty reporting, and less explicit code/data access limit the gains but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidential support.
